In La Granja, players control small farms by the Alpich pond near the village of Esporles on the island of Mallorca. Over time, the players develop their farms and deliver goods to the village. Players are vying to earn the title of "La Granja" for their country estate! Over the course of 6 game rounds, players will expand their farm by adding fields, farm extensions, market barrows, and helpers. They will earn VPs by delivering goods to the village of Esporles. It is important to observe the actions of other players, manipulate turn order, and adjust your strategy based on the dice and cards. La Granja is a fascinating game that requires careful planning. Timing and speed is crucial. However, successful players must cope with the uncertainty of events during the game. The player who has earned the most victory points at the end of the game is the winner and new owner of the La Granja estate! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 1.1 The game revolves around doing 3 main things 2 Rounds 2.1 Scoring points 3 Gathering goods (Farm Phase) 3.1 (1.1) Playing a card 3.1.1 Playing a card as a farm extension 3.1.2 Playing a card as a field 3.1.3 Playing a card as a helper 3.1.4 Playing a card as a market barrow 3.2 (1.2) Getting Income 3.3 (1.3) Producing on your fields 3.4 (1.4) Producing Pig Offspring 3.5 (1.5) Buying Roof Tiles 4 Gathering Goods (Revenue Phase) 4.1 Revenue 1 effect 4.2 Revenue 2 effect 4.3 Revenue 3 effect 4.4 Revenue 4 effect 4.5 Revenue 5 effect 4.6 Revenue 6 effect 5 Delivering goods (Transportation phase) 5.1 Selecting a delivery token 5.2 Recalculating turn order 5.3 Carrying out deliveries 5.4 Extra deliveries 5.5 Craft Buildings 5.6 Market Barrows 6 Scoring phase 7 Anytime actions 7.1 Sell a good 7.2 Buy a good 7.3 Upgrade a good 7.4 Use a roof tile 7.5 Use a box (commodity) 7.6 Use a helper Overview In La Granja, players earn points by getting goods and delivering them to central buildings, or their own personal orders. The game is played over 6 rounds as players try to use their cards effectively, as every card can be played four different ways! The game revolves around doing 3 main things Gathering goods for your personal farm Delivering goods to central buildings (craft buildings) or your own personal orders (market barrows) Getting abilities and improvements for gathering/delivering Gain as many points as possible over 6 rounds. The player with the most points is the winner. Rounds Each round consists of four phases: Farm phase (Blue) - play cards onto your farm, gain income, produce goods Revenue phase (Green) - roll dice to give extra benefits: gain income, produce goods, play/draw a card, get upgrades/siestas, gain deliveries Transportation phase (Gray) - gain delivery tokens and deliver goods to market barrows or craft buildings Scoring phase - gain points and update turn order In addition to the phases, there are several Anytime actions that can be taken during or between the phases. These can set the players up so that they can do something useful in the phases. They are the only time that goods can be upgraded (from raw to processed materials) so that they can be subsequently delivered as a processed material. Scoring points Points can be gained by: Delivering all goods to complete a market barrow (scores points shown in the hexagon) Delivering all goods to complete a row in a craft building (scores various points) Removing other players tokens from the central market board (scores 1 point per token removed) Having tokens on the central market board at the end of a round (scores 1 point per token) Being on the siesta track at the end of a round Gathering goods (Farm Phase) There are several ways to gather goods during the game. [Rating: 1/10] Boring, ugly, long & tedious piece of crap.  This game represents everything that is wrong with modern euro game.  Been there, done that ! I'm just so sick of those kind of crappy games.

[Rating: 1/10] Have you ever wondered to yourself "I wish I knew what it would be like to run every single aspect of a European farm and feel just as exhausted and bored by it as it sounds?" Well have I got the game for you!

[Rating: 1/10] Loathesome attitude from one of the designers to various rules questions in the forums.  Also unless you have a VERY specific set of circumstances, just go crates delivery 1-5 and ignore market barrow till the end. Donkey roofs > all.

[Rating: 2/10] This game has multiple bad flaws to it. The cards have no balance. Some are just better then others. There is no real way to manipulate what cards you get.   In the mid/end game it devolves into a war game for control of market spaces. How and why this makes any sense I don't know. But the result is it is like any other multiplayer war game.   The use of the cards for multiple different things is interesting, but in the end because only the market side is super important, it's not necessary and just gimmicky.   The open market area doesn't work very well. I guess it's just a clearing house for

[Rating: 2/10] La Granja is the antithesis of elegant. It lacks streamlining and polish in pretty much every way. No single element is captivating. Nothing fits together properly. Systems flow between each other nonsensically. Any semblance of theme is lost after leaving the player boards. Tactical when it should be strategic; strategic when it should be tactical. I hate this game and how cludgy it feels. I expect it to be someone's grail game though

[Rating: 2/10] Another comment nailed it:  "Too easy to get the resources you need, when you need it. Many upgrade options, or just pay cash. Dice selection for revenue usually always gives you what you want since you get five dice to put on six slots. Very telling that there wasn't one time during our die selection phase where I thought "oh no, she took the die I really wanted!" There was never any tension. Very gentle, very forgiving, solitary experience with little interaction, except for the market square where you push out other workers. Makes zero thematic sense."  I will add that it runs long for what

[Rating: 2/10] I tried this at Gencon.  No one at our table understood the rules after about 30 minutes of explaining it and over an hour of play.  We were saved by the hall's closing hours and only 2 turns had passed.  I do believe running a real farm and controlling the agricultural market would be both easier and more rewarding.

[Rating: 2/10] Eh, tracks over here, convert this here, what the heck is going on, I don't really care. Multi-use cards, yeah, sure. +1 here, +3-2 here.

[Rating: 2/10] Felt very restricted in what I could do. But in a bad way? Not an Agricola (tight gameplay) kind of way. Game was long and felt very boring.

[Rating: 3/10] Boring euro point salad. It's been a while since I was underwhelmed this much. Will not play again.

[Rating: 3/10] After all of the positivity and comparisons to euro games that I love, I was really surprised by how much I disliked this one.  This game does have the feel of a Feld game, as any review will tell you, but that can both be a good and bad thing. For me this game highlights the bad aspects of Feld games. You have a set of actions that you can do (buy goods, upgrade goods, make deliveries, gain money, etc.) and you just chain those actions together the best that you can. If I need to do action A, first I have to do action B, C, then D, and now I finally have what I need so that I can do action A.

[Rating: 3/10] I am a Eurogamer, but this game was just painful!   Unclear cards and unclear rules (6 pages of rules questions on BGG!) Fiddly as hell Waaay too many mechanisms in play Downtime off the chart Waaayyy to long! (took us over 3 hours) Connection to theme is negative, it's counterthematic!  The game in my opinion need to be cleaned up in so many ways, it's for me unbelivible that it has been released in this condition.
